canonical_title: Roll axis response in hovering flight
subject_group: 6.1.10 Vertical/short takeoff and landing air vehicles

versions.title_at_revision: Roll axis response in hovering flight
versions.text: Criterion: Verify that roll axis response in hovering flight is safe. Standard: The air vehicle meets the standards within MIL-STD-1797, 5.2.7.2.1.2 Roll axis response in hovering flight (see table XCII for guidance). Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test, demonstration, simulation, and inspection of process, design, test, or configuration documentation.

versions.title_at_revision: Roll axis response in hovering flight
versions.text:
Standard: The air vehicle hover roll response is no worse than Level 2 as specified in MIL-STD- 1797, Roll Axis Response in Hovering Flight paragraph and Angular (Moment-Generating) Control Power in Hovering Flight paragraph, unless pilot evaluation determines the air vehicle handling qualities are no worse than Level 2. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Analysis.
(1) Conduct analysis of all hover roll response to evaluate air vehicle capabilities and control margins, to include: a. Baseline control system. b. Precision hover modes. Test.
  (1) Lab test: Conduct flight test to assess flying/handling qualities as specified in MIL-STD- 1797, Roll Axis Response in Hovering Flight paragraph for each combination of air vehicle states, control modes, and environmental conditions, to include: a. Baseline control system. b. Precision hover modes. c. For control systems which automatically control pitch attitude, pilot will assess overall workload, pilot compensation, and any undesirable coupling of pitch response into other axes. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
  (2) Flight test: Conduct flight test to assess flying/handling qualities as specified in MIL-STD- 1797, Roll Axis Response in Hovering Flight paragraph for selected combinations of air vehicle states, control modes, and environmental conditions, to include: a. Baseline control system. b. Precision hover modes. c. For control systems which automatically control pitch attitude, pilot will assess overall workload, pilot compensation, and any undesirable coupling of pitch response into other axes.
